ladder.title: Two centres force many distances
ladder.q:
Let $P$ be a set of $n\ge 2$ points in the plane and let $t$ be the number of distinct values of $|p-q|$ with $p\ne q$ in $P$.

Show that $t\ge\sqrt{(n-2)/2}$.
ladder.source: P. Erdős, On sets of distances of n points, Amer. Math. Monthly 53 (1946), 248–250 (where a slightly stronger bound is proved); J. Pach & P. K. Agarwal, Combinatorial Geometry, Wiley 1995
ladder.note: The first lower bound of order $\sqrt n$ for distinct distances; everything later in the ladder improves the exponent towards $1$.

ladder.title: Unit distances via forbidden K(2,3)
ladder.q:
Let $P$ be a set of $n$ points in the plane and let $u(P)$ be the number of unordered pairs $\{p,q\}\subseteq P$ with $|p-q|=1$.

Show that $u(P)\le \frac{n}{4}\left(1+\sqrt{8n-7}\right)$. In particular $u(P)=O(n^{3/2})$.
ladder.source: J. Pach & P. K. Agarwal, Combinatorial Geometry, Wiley 1995; P. Brass, W. Moser & J. Pach, Research Problems in Discrete Geometry, Springer 2005
ladder.note: The trivial graph-theoretic bound (two unit circles meet in at most two points); the incidence method below lowers the exponent from $3/2$ to $4/3$.

ladder.title: The grid has few distinct distances
ladder.q:
Let $m\ge 2$, let $n=m^2$ and let $G=\{1,\dots,m\}^2\subseteq\mathbb{R}^2$.

You may use Landau's theorem: the number of integers in $[1,x]$ that are sums of two squares is asymptotic to $Kx/\sqrt{\log x}$ for some constant $K>0$. Show that there is an absolute constant $C$ such that $G$ determines at most $Cn/\sqrt{\log n}$ distinct distances.
ladder.source: P. Erdős, On sets of distances of n points, Amer. Math. Monthly 53 (1946), 248–250
ladder.note: This is the construction behind Erdős's conjecture that $n/\sqrt{\log n}$ is the truth for distinct distances.

ladder.title: Cauchy–Schwarz bound for point–line incidences
ladder.q:
Let $P$ be a set of $n$ points and $L$ a set of $m$ lines in the plane, and let $I(P,L)$ be the number of pairs $(p,\ell)\in P\times L$ with $p\in\ell$.

Show that $I(P,L)\le n\sqrt m+m$ and $I(P,L)\le m\sqrt n+n$.
ladder.source: J. Matoušek, Lectures on Discrete Geometry, Springer 2002; J. Pach & P. K. Agarwal, Combinatorial Geometry, Wiley 1995
ladder.note: The naive incidence bound; the Szemerédi–Trotter theorem replaces it by the sharp $n^{2/3}m^{2/3}$.

ladder.title: The crossing lemma
ladder.q:
For a simple graph $G$ let $\mathrm{cr}(G)$ be the minimum, over all drawings of $G$ in the plane, of the number of pairs of edges that cross.

Show that if $G$ has $v$ vertices and $e\ge 4v$ edges then $\mathrm{cr}(G)\ge \dfrac{e^3}{64v^2}$.
ladder.source: M. Ajtai, V. Chvátal, M. Newborn & E. Szemerédi, Crossing-free subgraphs, Ann. Discrete Math. 12 (1982), 9–12; F. T. Leighton, Complexity Issues in VLSI, MIT Press 1983; the constant 1/64 comes from the probabilistic proof in M. Aigner & G. M. Ziegler, Proofs from THE BOOK
ladder.note: The tool that gives one-paragraph proofs of the incidence and distance bounds that follow.

ladder.title: Szemerédi–Trotter theorem
ladder.q:
With $I(P,L)$ as before, show that there is an absolute constant $C$ such that for every set $P$ of $n$ points and every set $L$ of $m$ lines in the plane

$$I(P,L)\le C\left(n^{2/3}m^{2/3}+n+m\right).$$
ladder.source: E. Szemerédi & W. T. Trotter, Extremal problems in discrete geometry, Combinatorica 3 (1983), 381–392; proof via the crossing lemma in L. A. Székely, Crossing numbers and hard Erdős problems in discrete geometry, Combin. Probab. Comput. 6 (1997), 353–358
ladder.note: The sharp incidence bound; it is the engine for rich lines, unit distances and distinct distances.

ladder.title: Rich lines and Beck's theorem
ladder.q:
Let $P$ be a set of $n$ points in the plane.

(a) Show that there is an absolute constant $C$ such that for every $2\le k\le n$ the number of lines containing at least $k$ points of $P$ is at most $C\left(\dfrac{n^2}{k^3}+\dfrac nk\right)$.

(b) Show that there is an absolute constant $c>0$ such that either some line contains at least $cn$ points of $P$, or at least $cn^2$ distinct lines each contain at least two points of $P$.
ladder.source: E. Szemerédi & W. T. Trotter, Extremal problems in discrete geometry, Combinatorica 3 (1983), 381–392; J. Beck, On the lattice property of the plane and some problems of Dirac, Motzkin and Erdős in combinatorial geometry, Combinatorica 3 (1983), 281–297
ladder.note: Part (a) is exactly Erdős #1069 and part (b) is the case of #211 with $k$ proportional to $n$; #101 and #588 ask to beat the $O(n^2)$ that (a) gives for $4$-rich lines.

ladder.title: Unit distances: the n^{4/3} bound
ladder.q: Show that there is an absolute constant $C$ such that any $n$ points in the plane determine at most $Cn^{4/3}$ unordered pairs at distance exactly $1$.
ladder.source: J. Spencer, E. Szemerédi & W. T. Trotter, Unit distances in the Euclidean plane, in Graph Theory and Combinatorics (B. Bollobás, ed.), Academic Press 1984, 293–303
ladder.note: Still the best known upper bound for unit distances; Erdős conjectured $n^{1+O(1/\log\log n)}$, and #96 asks for $O(n)$ in convex position.

ladder.title: Pinned distinct distances: n^{4/5}
ladder.q:
Show that there is an absolute constant $c>0$ such that every set $P$ of $n\ge 2$ points in the plane contains a point $p$ with

$$\#\{\,|p-q| : q\in P\setminus\{p\}\,\}\ge c\,n^{4/5}.$$
ladder.source: L. A. Székely, Crossing numbers and hard Erdős problems in discrete geometry, Combin. Probab. Comput. 6 (1997), 353–358
ladder.note: A pinned bound from one point, from the crossing lemma applied to a multigraph of circle arcs; #604 asks for $n^{1-o(1)}$ distances from one point.

ladder.title: Guth–Katz: distance energy and n/log n distances
ladder.q:
Let $P$ be a set of $n\ge 2$ points in the plane.

Show that the number of quadruples $(a,b,c,d)\in P^4$ with $|a-b|=|c-d|\ne 0$ is at most $Cn^3\log n$, and deduce that $P$ determines at least $c\,n/\log n$ distinct distances. Here $C,c>0$ are absolute constants.
ladder.source: L. Guth & N. H. Katz, On the Erdős distinct distances problem in the plane, Ann. of Math. 181 (2015), 155–190, arXiv:1011.4105
ladder.note: The energy bound settles #95 and leaves only a $\sqrt{\log n}$ gap to the grid construction in #89.

ladder.title: Infinite Ramsey theorem
ladder.q:
Show that $\aleph_0\to(\aleph_0)^n_r$ for all positive integers $n$ and $r$: for every colouring of the $n$-element subsets of $\mathbb{N}$ with $r$ colours there is an infinite $H\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ all of whose $n$-element subsets have the same colour.

Deduce that every sequence of distinct real numbers has an infinite strictly monotone subsequence.
ladder.source: F. P. Ramsey, On a problem of formal logic, Proc. London Math. Soc. (2) 30 (1930), 264–286; R. L. Graham, B. L. Rothschild & J. H. Spencer, Ramsey Theory, Wiley
ladder.note: The basic positive arrow relation that every rung below generalises to ordinals, uncountable cardinals or graphs.

ladder.title: Decomposable ordinals fail the triangle arrow
ladder.q:
For an ordinal $\alpha$ write $\alpha\to(\alpha,3)^2$ if for every red/blue colouring of the $2$-element subsets of $\alpha$ there is either a subset of order type $\alpha$ all of whose pairs are red, or a $3$-element subset all of whose pairs are blue.

Show that if $\alpha=\beta+\gamma$ for ordinals $\beta,\gamma<\alpha$, then $\alpha\not\to(\alpha,3)^2$. Conclude that every ordinal $\alpha\ge 2$ with $\alpha\to(\alpha,3)^2$ is of the form $\omega^\delta$ with $\delta\ge 1$.
ladder.source: F. Galvin & J. Larson, Pinning countable ordinals, Fund. Math. 82 (1974/75), 357–361
ladder.note: It explains why Erdős #590–592 only concern ordinals of the form $\omega^\beta$.

ladder.title: Sierpiński's colouring
ladder.q: Show that $2^{\aleph_0}\not\to(\aleph_1)^2_2$: there is a colouring of the $2$-element subsets of $\mathbb{R}$ with two colours such that no subset of $\mathbb{R}$ of cardinality $\aleph_1$ has all its $2$-element subsets of the same colour.
ladder.source: W. Sierpiński, Sur un problème de la théorie des relations, Ann. Scuola Norm. Sup. Pisa (2) 2 (1933), 285–287; T. Jech, Set Theory (3rd ed., Springer 2003), Ch. 9
ladder.note: The first negative arrow: Ramsey's theorem does not go up from $\aleph_0$ to the continuum.

ladder.title: The shift graph
ladder.q:
Let $\kappa=(2^{\aleph_0})^+$. Let $G$ be the graph whose vertices are the pairs $(\alpha,\beta)$ of ordinals with $\alpha<\beta<\kappa$, in which $(\alpha,\beta)$ is adjacent to $(\beta,\gamma)$ whenever $\alpha<\beta<\gamma<\kappa$, and there are no other edges.

Show that $G$ contains no triangle and that $G$ has no proper vertex colouring with countably many colours.
ladder.source: P. Erdős & A. Hajnal, On chromatic number of infinite graphs, in Theory of Graphs (Proc. Colloq. Tihany 1966), Academic Press 1968, 83–98
ladder.note: So triangles are not forced by uncountable chromatic number, which is half of the graph case of #593.

ladder.title: Erdős–Rado for pairs
ladder.q: Show that $(2^{\aleph_0})^+\to(\aleph_1)^2_{\aleph_0}$: for every colouring of the $2$-element subsets of a set of cardinality $(2^{\aleph_0})^+$ with countably many colours there is a subset of cardinality $\aleph_1$ all of whose $2$-element subsets have the same colour.
ladder.source: P. Erdős & R. Rado, A partition calculus in set theory, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 62 (1956), 427–489
ladder.note: Together with Sierpiński's colouring it shows that $(2^{\aleph_0})^+$ is the least cardinal with this property; #1167 asks how such stepping-up relations transfer between exponents.

ladder.title: Obligatory graphs are exactly the bipartite ones
ladder.q: Show that a finite graph $H$ is isomorphic to a subgraph of every graph with chromatic number greater than $\aleph_0$ if and only if $H$ is bipartite.
ladder.source: P. Erdős & A. Hajnal, On chromatic number of graphs and set-systems, Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. 17 (1966), 61–99; stated as Theorem 1.1 in C. Reiher, Obligatory hypergraphs, arXiv:2403.11223
ladder.note: This completely answers the graph analogue of #593, which asks the same question for $3$-uniform hypergraphs.

ladder.title: Specker's theorem on omega squared
ladder.q: With the notation $\alpha\to(\alpha,3)^2$ from above, show that $\omega^2\to(\omega^2,3)^2$, and that $\omega^n\not\to(\omega^n,3)^2$ for every integer $n\ge 3$.
ladder.source: E. Specker, Teilmengen von Mengen mit Relationen, Comment. Math. Helv. 31 (1957), 302–314
ladder.note: It settles the finite exponents $\beta$ in #592 and shows the answer is not monotone in $\beta$.

ladder.title: Large odd cycles in uncountably chromatic graphs
ladder.q: Let $G$ be a graph with chromatic number greater than $\aleph_0$. Show that there is a positive integer $k$ such that $G$ contains a cycle of length $\ell$ for every odd $\ell\ge k$.
ladder.source: P. Erdős, A. Hajnal & S. Shelah, On some general properties of chromatic numbers, in Topics in Topology (Proc. Colloq. Keszthely 1972), Colloq. Math. Soc. János Bolyai 8, North-Holland 1974, 243–255
ladder.note: No fixed odd cycle is forced, but all long ones are; #1067 and #1068 ask which further structure (high connectivity) uncountable chromatic number forces.

ladder.title: Chang's theorem
ladder.q: Show that $\omega^\omega\to(\omega^\omega,3)^2$.
ladder.source: C. C. Chang, A partition theorem for the complete graph on ω^ω, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 12 (1972), 396–452
ladder.note: The first infinite exponent $\beta=\omega$ in #592, answering #590.

ladder.title: Schipperus: two indecomposable summands
ladder.q:
Let $\gamma\ge 1$ be a countable ordinal that is the sum of one or two additively indecomposable ordinals. Show that

$$\omega^{\omega^\gamma}\to(\omega^{\omega^\gamma},3)^2.$$
ladder.source: R. Schipperus, Countable partition ordinals, Ann. Pure Appl. Logic 161 (2010), 1195–1215
ladder.note: With $\gamma=2=1+1$ this answers #591; Schipperus also showed that it fails when $\gamma$ is a sum of four or more indecomposables, so three summands is the open case of #592.

ladder.title: Divisibility pairs in the first 2n integers
ladder.q: Let $n\ge 1$. Show that among any $n+1$ distinct integers from $\{1,\dots,2n\}$ one divides another, and find $n$ distinct integers in $\{1,\dots,2n\}$ none of which divides another.
ladder.source: M. Aigner & G. M. Ziegler, Proofs from THE BOOK, chapter on pigeon-hole and double counting
ladder.note: The model argument: pigeonhole on a multiplicative invariant (the odd part).

ladder.title: Zero-sum subsets modulo n
ladder.q:
Let $n\ge 1$ and let $a_1,\dots,a_n$ be integers. Show that there is a nonempty $S\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}$ with $n\mid\sum_{i\in S}a_i$.

Show that the statement can fail for $n-1$ integers.
ladder.source: M. Aigner & G. M. Ziegler, Proofs from THE BOOK, chapter on pigeon-hole and double counting
ladder.note: The simplest zero-sum statement; the Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv and Erdős–Heilbronn rungs ask for zero sums with extra constraints.

ladder.title: A square from exponent vectors
ladder.q:
Let $p_1,\dots,p_k$ be primes and let $a_1,\dots,a_{k+1}$ be positive integers all of whose prime factors lie in $\{p_1,\dots,p_k\}$. Show that there is a nonempty $S\subseteq\{1,\dots,k+1\}$ such that $\prod_{i\in S}a_i$ is a perfect square.

Show that $k$ such integers need not have this property.
ladder.source: R. Crandall & C. Pomerance, Prime Numbers: A Computational Perspective (2nd ed., Springer 2005)
ladder.note: Linear algebra on exponent vectors mod 2; problems on square products such as #437 and #841 start here.

ladder.title: Sperner bound for subset sums
ladder.q: Let $a_1,\dots,a_N$ be positive real numbers (not necessarily distinct) and let $t\in\mathbb{R}$. Show that the number of sets $S\subseteq\{1,\dots,N\}$ with $\sum_{i\in S}a_i=t$ is at most $\binom{N}{\lfloor N/2\rfloor}$, and that equality can occur.
ladder.source: P. Erdős, On a lemma of Littlewood and Offord, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 51 (1945), 898–902
ladder.note: The order $2^N/\sqrt N$ is right when repeated values are allowed; #362 asks what happens when the $a_i$ are distinct.

ladder.title: Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv theorem
ladder.q: Let $n\ge 1$. Show that among any $2n-1$ integers (not necessarily distinct) there are $n$ whose sum is divisible by $n$, and that $2n-2$ integers do not suffice in general.
ladder.source: P. Erdős, A. Ginzburg & A. Ziv, Theorem in the additive number theory, Bull. Res. Council Israel 10F (1961), 41–43
ladder.note: A zero-sum theorem with a prescribed number of terms; #541 asks about residue sequences whose zero-sum subsets all have the same size.

ladder.title: Zero-sum-free sets have size O(sqrt N)
ladder.q:
Show that there is an absolute constant $C$ such that, for every $N\ge 1$, every set $A\subseteq\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$ of distinct residues with $|A|\ge C\sqrt N$ has a nonempty subset $S$ with $\sum_{s\in S}s\equiv 0\pmod N$.

Show also that for every $N\ge 1$ there is a set of more than $\sqrt{2N}-2$ distinct nonzero residues modulo $N$ with no nonempty subset summing to $0$ modulo $N$.
ladder.source: E. Szemerédi, On a conjecture of Erdős and Heilbronn, Acta Arith. 17 (1970), 227–229
ladder.note: This answers Erdős #540 up to the constant; Balandraud (Israel J. Math. 2012) found the sharp threshold for prime $N$.

ladder.title: Sárközy–Szemerédi: subset sums of distinct integers
ladder.q: Show that there is an absolute constant $C$ such that, for every $N\ge 1$, every set $A$ of $N$ distinct positive integers and every integer $t$, the number of $S\subseteq A$ with $\sum_{s\in S}s=t$ is at most $C\,2^N N^{-3/2}$.
ladder.source: A. Sárközy & E. Szemerédi, Über ein Problem von Erdős und Moser, Acta Arith. 11 (1965), 205–208
ladder.note: Having distinct elements saves a factor of $N$ over the Sperner bound; this answers Erdős #362 (the Erdős–Moser problem).

ladder.title: Graham's gcd conjecture
ladder.q:
Let $n\ge 1$ and let $a_1<a_2<\dots<a_n$ be positive integers. Show that there exist indices $i,j$ with

$$\frac{a_i}{\gcd(a_i,a_j)}\ge n.$$
ladder.source: R. Balasubramanian & K. Soundararajan, On a conjecture of R. L. Graham, Acta Arith. 75 (1996), 1–38
ladder.note: This is exactly the statement of Erdős #402, conjectured by Graham and proved for all $n$ by Balasubramanian and Soundararajan.

ladder.title: Cameron–Erdős: counting sum-free sets
ladder.q:
Let $f(N)$ be the number of sets $A\subseteq\{1,\dots,N\}$, the empty set included, such that there are no $a,b,c\in A$ (not necessarily distinct) with $a+b=c$.

Show that there is an absolute constant $C$ such that $f(N)\le C\,2^{N/2}$ for all $N\ge 1$.
ladder.source: B. Green, The Cameron–Erdős conjecture, Bull. London Math. Soc. 36 (2004), 769–778
ladder.note: This gives a much sharper form of Erdős #748: the subsets of the odd numbers and of the top half already give at least $2^{\lceil N/2\rceil}$ sum-free sets, so the order of magnitude is exact.

ladder.title: No term divides the sum of two larger terms
ladder.q:
Let $N\ge 1$ and let $A\subseteq\{1,\dots,N\}$ be such that there are no $a,b,c\in A$, with $b=c$ allowed, satisfying $a<\min(b,c)$ and $a\mid b+c$.

Show that $|A|\le N/3+C$ for an absolute constant $C$, and check that the set of integers in $(2N/3,N]$ satisfies the hypothesis.
ladder.source: B. Bedert, On a problem of Erdős and Sárközy about sequences with no term dividing the sum of two larger terms, arXiv:2301.07065 (2023)
ladder.note: This settles the finite problem #13; #12 asks for the corresponding infinite sets, where much less is known.
